# Item Corruption

by VisionGLLast Updated: March 25, 2026

### Advertisement

This website is supported by ads.

## What is Item Corruption?

Item Corruption
Item Corruption involves using Rune of Corruption to unpredictably change an item, for better or worse. Additionally, Corrupt Items can drop as loot from Omen Window encounters. A Corrupt Item can't be modified in any way, other than through the use of Rune of Shattering or a Sacrificial Altar. The results of Item Corruption can range from altering the tiers and values of Affixes, changing the item to a new Subtype, or even making the item Unequippable.

## Obtaining Corrupt Items

Item Corruption
Corrupt Items are crafted using Runes of Corruption or dropped naturally as loot from Omen Windows. You can also purchase Crates of Corrupted Items from Apophis the Oracle using Timeglass Fragments.

### Rune of Corruption Crafting

Runes of Corruption are crafting materials dropped from Omen Windows or purchased with Timeglass Fragment from Apophis the Oracle. Like other Runes, Runes of Corruption are used in the Forge to modify equipment.

Rune of Corruption

## Results of Item Corruption

Item Corruption
When Corrupting an Item, there are several outcomes to consider. First, Corrupting an Item is permanent and removes the ability to further modify the item in any way. The only exceptions are using Rune of Shattering or destroying it at a Sacrificial Altar. Additionally, Corrupting an Item can alter it in various ways.

There are five different categories of outcomes obtainable through Item Corruption:

- An item can have its Affix Tiers or Values changed.
- Affixes can be removed or added.
- The Rarity of the Item can be altered.
- The item Subtype can change.
- The item can become Unequippable.

### Amulets and Attribute Corruption

Corrupting an Amulet has a chance to add an Affix that converts existing Attributes to new Corrupted Attributes with different effects.

These are the five Corrupted Attributes and their associated effects:

- Vitality converted to Rampancy
- Rampancy:
- 3% increased Effectiveness of Frenzy per point.
- 0.1% More Damage Taken while you don’t have Frenzy per point.

- Strength converted to Brutality
- Brutality:
- 0.02% More Damage for Melee attacks per 1 Mana cost (up to max 20, multiplicative with other modifiers) per point.
- Globally reduces Health Leech by 0.5% per point.

- Dexterity converted to Guile
- Guile:
- 0.3% Cooldown Recovery Speed for Movement Skills per point.
- 1% reduced Armor per point.

- Intelligence converted to Madness
- Madness:
- 1% Spell Critical Multiplier per point.
- 1% increased Bonus Damage Taken from Critical Strikes per point.

- Attunement converted to Apathy
- Apathy:
- 2% increased Mana Regeneration per point
- 0.2% of Current Health lost when you directly use a Skill per point.

### New Item Subtypes

Some Item Subtypes are only available through Item Corruption. Corrupted Item Subtypes have unique Implicits that have one beneficial effect and one drawback.

These are the Corrupted Item Subtypes that are currently available:

- Singularity Belt
- Only has one Potion slot by default, but restores an Evade charge when you use a Potion.

- Corruption Binding
- Has 8 Potion slots by default, but reduces Health Gained on Potion Use by 31-37%.

- Deadstar Amulet
- Gives 20-24% Less Damage Over Time Taken, increases your Damage Over Time by 42-60%, but reduces Armor by 42-60%.

- Cursed Coin Amulet
- Gives 51-83% Lightning Resistance, and +1 to All Skills, but 4-5% Increased Damage Taken.

- Corrupted Insignia
- Gives 13-19% Increased Cooldown Recovery Speed for Evade, 3-4 seconds of Frenzy after you use Evade, but 6-7% Increased Damage Taken while you have Frenzy.

- Opal Eye Ring
- Gives 6-10% Increased Cooldown Recovery Speed, and 6-7 to All Attributes, but reduces Movement Speed by 6-7%.

- Timeglass Chalice
- Non-class specific Relic that grants 23-31 Mana and 23-31% increased Mana Regen, but reduces Health Regen by 31-47%.

- Doom Gourd
- Primalist Relic that adds 11-17 Minion Melee Void Damage and Minion Spell Void Damage, but reduces Minion Physical Resistance by 11-17%.

- Aberrant Eye
- Mage Relic that grants 7-13 Ward per Second, and 11-13% of Maximum Health gained as Ward Decay Threshold, but reduces Health by 7-9%.

- Apocalypse Code
- Sentinel Relic that grants 13-17% Physical and Void Penetration, but reduces Health by 5-7%.

- Prophetic Homonculus
- Acolyte Relic that grants 61-77% Necrotic and Void Resistance, but reduces Armor by 37-47%.

- Bottled Time
- Rogue Relic that grants 6-12% Increased Movement Speed and Cooldown Recovery Speed, but increases Damage over Time Taken by 12-24%.

## When to Corrupt an Item

Item Corruption
Since the results of Item Corruption are permanent, it's important to consider the decision first. Be sure to have a backup Item in place in case the Corruption fails, and never Corrupt an Item that your build needs to function or that you aren't ready to lose. With that being said, there are some instances where using a Rune of Corruption can be beneficial.

### Build Enabling Item Subtypes

If your build uses a specific Corrupted Item Subtype to enhance it, consider Corrupting early and often to find the Item Subtype you're looking for. Corrupted Item Subtypes, such as Cursed Coin Amulet's +1 to All Skills or Bottled Time's Increased Cooldown Recovery Speed, can help bring a build online.

### Gaining Power

When you are pushing to take your Build up in power, Item Corruption is an option to consider. Item Corruption's possibility to raise the values of Affix Tiers or add new and useful Affixes can help squeeze extra power out of gear you already have. However, with the risks also associated with Item Corrupting, it's important to have a backup Item to take its place, should your attempt to make a better Item fail.

### For the Thrill

The results of Item Corruption are wild and varied. Making the decision to use a Rune of Corruption invites countless possibilities, both beneficial and detrimental. If you notice your Runes of Corruption piling up in your inventory, you could choose to tempt fate and take the risk. There is always the possibility that your newly acquired Corrupt Item is the perfect fit for a future Build.

## Summary

Item Corruption
- Corrupt Items are made using Rune of Corruption, found as loot drops from Omen Window encounters, or acquired from Corrupt Item Crates.
- Rune of Corruption is found by completing Omen Window encounters, or by purchasing them from Apophis the Oracle using Timeglass Fragment.
- You can't modify a Corrupt Item. Destroying the item with a Rune of Shattering or a Sacrificial Altar is the only exception.
- Corruption can change Affix Tiers or Values, add or remove Affixes, change the Rarity of items, change the Subtype of an item, or make an item Unequippable.
- Corrupting Amulets has a chance to add an Affix that Corrupts Attributes, changing them to new types with new effects.
- Some Item Subtypes are only available through Corruption.
- Item Corruption is a powerful tool for enabling Builds and increasing power, but it comes with significant risks.
